definitions.gloss: standpoint; viewpoint; perspective from which to consider something
definitions.explanation: The position or angle from which one considers an issue. Used in formal contexts to indicate the framework or set of values guiding analysis.

examples.japanese: {法律|ほうりつ}の{見地|けんち}から{説明|せつめい}した。
examples.english: I explained it from a legal standpoint.

examples.japanese: {教育|きょういく}の{見地|けんち}から{見|み}ると、この{制度|せいど}は{問題|もんだい}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: From an educational standpoint, this system has many problems.

examples.japanese: {長期的|ちょうきてき}な{見地|けんち}に{立|た}って{判断|はんだん}する{必要|ひつよう}がある。
examples.english: We need to make a judgment from a long-term perspective.

notes:
Formal; common in academic, legal, business, and policy discussion. Most often appears in the patterns ～の{見地|けんち}から ("from the standpoint of ~") and ～の{見地|けんち}に{立|た}つ ("to take the standpoint of ~").

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ～の{見地|けんち}から: from the standpoint of ~
- {見地|けんち}に{立|た}つ: to take the standpoint
- {法律|ほうりつ}の{見地|けんち}: legal standpoint
- {長期的|ちょうきてき}な{見地|けんち}: long-term perspective

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {観点|かんてん}: viewpoint — very close in meaning and more common in everyday speech
- {立場|たちば}: position; standpoint — emphasizes one's social role or situation rather than analytical framework
- {視点|してん}: viewpoint; angle — focuses on where one's eyes are placed, more literal/visual
